overview.explanation: Solid arrows show the order of guards and permitted accepted transitions. An invalid or busy return ends that call without changing queued. This is a bounded state model, not a running network service.

focus.title: Return an explicit outcome
focus.code:
enum class Outcome{accepted,invalid,busy};unsigned queued=0;
    auto submit=[&](int n){if(n<0||n>100)return Outcome::invalid;if(queued==2)return Outcome::busy;++queued;return Outcome::accepted;};
explain: enum class declares a scoped set of named outcomes. Callers use names such as Outcome::busy. queued is an unsigned count initialized to zero.
[&] borrows queued. The invalid guard has priority, then the full guard. Only acceptance increments the count. Each return ends the current submit call.
focus.what: An outcome value says why a request was or was not admitted.
focus.where: This lambda is the admission boundary of the toy service model.
focus.why: Callers can respond differently to invalid work and temporary lack of space without inspecting internal state.
focus.invariant: The count remains in 0–2. Rejected requests do not change it. Invalid input is reported as invalid even when capacity is full.
focus.risk: Treating busy as accepted would mislead callers. Concurrent access would race without synchronization, and a real queue would also need completion/removal behavior.

focus.title: Make outcomes observable
explain: The capture-free lambda maps an Outcome to a string_view of a string literal. The trailing -> states the result type; the ?: operators choose the text. String literals live for the program’s lifetime.
The colon introduces a range-based loop. n is a value copy of each array element: 2, -1, 3, 4. Submit and format each outcome, then print a newline.
focus.what: The fixture prints accepted, invalid, accepted, busy on four lines.
focus.where: Formatting happens after each call returns its typed outcome.
focus.why: Readable results allow tests and callers to distinguish rejection reasons.
focus.invariant: The string_view must refer to live text; here it refers to string literals. The count ends at two.
focus.risk: Returning a string_view of a temporary string would dangle. Adding a new enum value requires reviewing the formatter, whose last branch currently treats any remaining value as busy.
